question: After accounting for the number of candidate species x site cells, does rainfall preferentially reactivate full choruses at physical sites where the same species has been recorded in other years?
population: Frozen NAAMP matched pairs restricted to pairs with identical nonmissing SiteID at all ten StopNumbers.
candidate_cells: Within each State x RouteNumber x RunNumber stratum, use the historical species pool represented in eligible runs. For a focal pair, candidate cells are candidate species absent from the entire dry route crossed with the ten stable physical SiteIDs.

memory_exposure.recurrent_cell: The same species was detected at the same SiteID in any other eligible run of the stratum, excluding the focal wet and dry runs.

outcome: wet_ci3 = 1 when the focal wet run has CallingIndex 3 for that candidate species at that SiteID, else 0.
pair_summary: For each pair, compute wet_ci3 rates separately among recurrent and nonrecurrent candidate cells; primary response is recurrent_rate - nonrecurrent_rate.

model.estimator: Weighted least squares on pair-level rate difference.
model.weight: n_recurrent * n_nonrecurrent / (n_recurrent + n_nonrecurrent), the effective two-group opportunity size.
model.formula: rate_difference ~ rain_contrast + temperature_difference + day_of_year_difference + year_gap + State + RunNumber
model.minimum_pair_opportunity: At least 5 candidate cells in each memory group.

minimum_gate: >=1500 eligible pairs and >=300 routes after the opportunity requirement.
sensitivities: Same-observer subset with the identical opportunity and model rules.
Repeat outcome as wet CallingIndex >=2 rather than exactly 3; directional diagnostic only.
interpretation: A positive rain coefficient means increasing rainfall contrast selectively increases chorus activation at previously used species-site combinations beyond their numerical availability.
This is stronger evidence for site-memory reactivation than a raw recurrent share alone.
It still does not prove continuous occupancy, individual identity, reproductive success, or a physiological mediator.
